CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up regarding recent hospitalization for infection, spasms, lightheadedness, and constipation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female with history of quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury admitted to District Regional Hospital from 06/29/2021 to 07/02/2021. Patient presented to the emergency department with increasing spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. She was febrile with elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. Patient had labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. Urinary tract infection was suspected and patient was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She has a supra-pubic catheter. Cultures were obtained. She slowly improved and was discharged after clinical improvement.

Patient attributes her hospitalization primarily to severe constipation and autonomic dysreflexia rather than true urinary tract infection. She notes that upon discharge and having a bowel movement at home, she felt significantly better. Patient states her blood pressure elevation and associated headache and vomiting resolved after bowel evacuation. She denies concerns about the elevated white blood cell count, questioning whether dysreflexia could have affected it. Urine cultures were not impressive. Patient reports feeling back to her normal self currently.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current pain or discomfort. Denies active spasms or lightheadedness. Denies current constipation issues.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury
History of autonomic dysreflexia
Constipation
Recent hospitalization for infection/constipation (06/29/2021-07/02/2021)

MEDICATIONS
Miralax daily
Lactulose as needed for severe constipation (patient reports it takes approximately 2 days to work)
Vitamin C
Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not documented

Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient tends to stay indoors more during hot weather. She is somewhat homeopathic in her health approach. Patient is unvaccinated against COVID-19 and expresses hesitancy regarding vaccination, citing concerns about unknown side effects and reports of "vaccine injury." She believes her young age and overall health status, along with vitamin supplementation and close monitoring, provide sufficient protection.

Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, normal breathing
General: Patient appears well
Abdomen: Not specifically documented

No acute distress noted

RESULTS
Recent hospitalization labs showed:
- White blood cell count: 23,000 (elevated)
- Urine cultures: Not impressive/negative
- X-rays performed during hospitalization
- Prior white blood cell count approximately one year ago: normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

ACUTE TO CHRONIC CONSTIPATION
Patient's recent hospitalization likely related to severe constipation with associated autonomic dysreflexia rather than true urinary tract infection. Current bowel regimen with daily Miralax and lactulose as rescue therapy appears effective. Patient reports good compliance with Miralax daily and doubling dose when needed.
Plan: Return for follow-up labs in 2-3 weeks including fasting complete blood count (CBC) and comprehensive metabolic panel with lipid panel. Will reassess white blood cell count to ensure it normalizes. Patient understands this will address both her leukocytosis and her due cholesterol monitoring. Discussed dehydration and heat-related exacerbation of constipation, particularly given the extreme heat during late June that preceded her hospitalization.

QUADRIPLEGIA
Continue current management and monitoring. Patient currently stable with no acute concerns.

COVID-19 VACCINE STATUS
Patient currently unvaccinated. Discussed at length. Physician recommends vaccination as patient is considered high-risk given quadriplegia and respiratory limitations. Explained that vaccine is safe and represents the only true preventative mechanism against COVID-19. Discussed that supplements are unlikely to provide meaningful protection. Reassured patient regarding vaccine safety based on extensive population vaccination data (50% of country vaccinated) and physician's personal experience and that of family members. Addressed patient's concerns about vaccine side effects, explaining these are rare (e.g., Guillain-Barré syndrome) compared to risks of COVID-19 infection. Counseled that pandemic trends suggest virus will become less deadly as it mutates. Patient is open-minded but remains hesitant. Patient to make own decision regarding vaccination. Encouraged patient to follow up with questions.
